title: Solitary waves of attracting SU(N) fermions
authors: Aysha Alsubaihi, Wayne J. Chetcuti, Frederic Chevy, Juan Polo, Luigi Amico
abstract: We study the formation, dynamics, and disorder robustness of bound states in attractively interacting SU(N) fermions on a one-dimensional ring lattice. Using exact diagonalization in fixed-momentum sectors and Bethe ansatz exact results as a guide, we resolve the many-body spectrum into bands related to the possible partitions of the particles into bound composites, and characterize their internal structure also through density-density and N-body correlations. A pinning quench protocol reveals a transition from dispersive spreading to dynamical localization as the attractive interaction increases relative to the single-particle hopping. We find that the bound state dynamics for one-particle per component occurs as a many-body quantum walk similar to that of a single particle with a re-normalized effective mass. Such a property, that is the quantum version of the shape-preserving motion of classical solitons, can provide the dynamical signature of the fermionic solitary waves. We probe the robustness of the fermionic bound-state dynamics under on-site disorder.
summary: The paper theoretically investigates solitary waves formed by attractively interacting SU(N) fermions on a lattice. It establishes that these bound states exhibit dynamics analogous to quantum walks, mirroring classical soliton behavior. The study also quantifies how disorder affects this confinement and derives effective hopping parameters for the composite excitations.
main_problem: The study investigates the formation, dynamics, and disorder robustness of bound states (solitary waves) in attractively interacting SU(N) fermions on a 1D lattice.
main_result: Bound states propagate as quantum walks, exhibiting a dynamical signature analogous to classical soliton motion. Furthermore, their confinement is shown to be enhanced by increasing the component number N under disorder.
method: The analysis employs exact diagonalization in fixed-momentum sectors and utilizes Bethe ansatz results for the dilute limit. Dynamics are probed via quench protocols and correlation functions.
model_or_system: The system models attractively interacting SU(N) fermions on a 1D ring lattice, governed by an extended Fermi-Hubbard type Hamiltonian. The continuum limit maps this to the Gaudin–Yang–Sutherland (GYS) model.
key_observables: Energy spectrum bands, density-density correlation $G(r)$, N-body correlator $T_N(r)$, and the Hellinger distance ($d_H$) comparing dynamics to single-particle quantum walks.
important_parameters: Attractive interaction strength $|U|$, hopping amplitude $J$, disorder strength $W$, and component number $N$ (SU(2), SU(3), etc.).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on mapping the lattice problem to integrable models in the dilute limit, and uses perturbative expansions for effective hopping in the strongly coupled regime.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate energy spectra showing distinct bound bands (Fig. 1, Fig. 6), density evolution confirming quantum walk behavior after rescaling time (Fig. 2), and correlation length decay under disorder (Fig. 3, Fig. 8).
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the lattice Hamiltonian and analyzing the energy spectrum via Bethe ansatz solutions to characterizing the dynamics using quench protocols and correlations. It then explores the continuum limit mapping and finally examines the robustness of these bound states against disorder.
why_interesting: This work connects concepts from integrable many-body physics (Bethe ansatz) with observable quantum transport phenomena (quantum walks), providing a detailed theoretical framework for understanding emergent collective excitations in strongly interacting fermionic systems relevant to ultracold atomic gases.

For legibility only every second momentum sector is included, and within each band every tenth eigenstate is plotted. Curves are colored by the composite configuration of their band.
